newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain loss from floods, rain seen 1 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain loss from floods, rain seen 1 mln T.

text.p: Poland's grain harvest might be cut by a total of one million tonnes due to the flooding and heavy rain that afflicted Poland in July, the president of the Warsaw branch of the PZZ grain firm said on Saturday.

Bogdan Judzinski told Reuters that he agreed with the agriculture ministry's estimate that flooding may have caused losses of 600,000-800,000 tonnes but said heavy rain on tall plants may have pushed the number to one million.

"My one-million-tonne estimate takes into consideration two things: losses caused by flooding...and losses from rain laying grain plants flat, harvesting by scythes rather than combines, and grain falling from ears," Judzinski told Reuters.
Analysts estimate Poland's 1997 grain output at between 23.6 and 24.7 million tonnes, the latter number the amount Poland produced last year.
Judzinski said that this year's grain harvest should be at about 25 million tonnes but noted that the Central Statistical Office (GUS) had yet to provide a figure.
The floods, which hit southwestern Poland nearly four weeks ago, killed 54 people and swamped more than 6,000 sq km including several cities.
There are 90 PZZ grain firms in Poland, about 70 percent of which have been privatised.
